keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. "At the height of its reach, the empire covered most of southern Somalia as well as eastern Ethiopia", "its domain at one point extending from Hobyo in the north to Kismayo in the south, and Qelafo in the west". The page does not date the height; the 16th century (Portuguese battles, the 1580s Ottoman-Somali offensive) is the span in which the page places the Ajuran at their strongest. No area figure on the page: the drawn region is about 0.9 M km2 (southern Somalia plus a 150 km disc at Qelafo), the Ethiopian part is not drawn beyond that disc.

notes:
New dossier: Cliopatria has no Ajuran row. Pages opened: Ajuran Sultanate, Sultanate of Mogadishu, Geledi Sultanate (3). The Ajuran page dates nothing but the infobox ("Established: 13th century", "Disestablished: 1695"), the late-1300s rise in the Banaadir, the 16th-century Portuguese battles and the mid-17th-century Oromo expansion; every start and extent date here is a century placeholder at confidence 1 or 2, and the extent (Hobyo to Kismayo and Qelafo) is the page's one geographic statement. The Hiraab Imamate (hiraab-imamate), the Geledi Sultanate (geledi-sultanate) and the Sultanate of Mogadishu (sultanate-of-mogadishu) are written in this batch; a gap-filler should open 'Gaal Madow' and a Somali history source for the extent over time.
The Sultanate of Mogadishu (city-state, 'founded mid-13th century or 1330') has its own treaty with the Portuguese in 1542 yet its page says it came under Ajuran control; the relation (vassal or not) and its dates are page-silent, so no vassal event is recorded. Counterpart string 'Oromo' has no dossier (the Oromo migrations are not a state). Disagreement: the infobox puts the Oromo invasions in the 16th century, the body in the mid-17th; the infobox ends the sultanate in 1695, the body at 'the end of the 17th century' and 'the early 1700s'.
Gazetteer names needed: Qelafo (Qalafo, about 5.6 N 44.2 E, Shabelle zone, Somali Region of Ethiopia; given as a coordinate), Hobyo (Xobyo, about 5.35 N 48.5 E), Mareeg (the place Mereeg is in the gazetteer; the capital's coordinate is its centroid).
